# Hypercolor 0.7.3

**Released:** 2026-10-25

Multi-zone scenes get a real preview. Every surface (web UI, TUI, Python SDK, and the WebSocket protocol itself) can now follow a single zone instead of the scene canvas patchwork, and the daemon only does preview work for zones somebody is actually watching. The rest of the release is render-pipeline correctness: black-frame regressions, log spam under persistent failures, and CI determinism.

## 🌟 Highlights

### ✨ Follow one zone in the main preview
Multi-zone scenes previously rendered as a scene canvas: every zone projected into its device layout box, which reads as an unusable patchwork. The web UI now shows one zone at a time, picked from the cabinet's zone chips on the Dashboard, Effects, and Studio pages. Pages without a zone picker fall back to the Primary zone rather than the patchwork. New `crates/hypercolor-ui/src/preview_zone.rs` holds the `PreviewZoneContext` and the derivation logic.

### ⚡️ Preview work scoped to selected zones
The daemon tracks a `ZonePreviewSelection` per subscriber and stages, reads back, and encodes only the **union** of what subscribers asked for. Watching one zone of a sixteen-zone scene costs one zone of GPU staging and readback, not sixteen. Unselected GPU zones skip staging, collection, and readback entirely.

### 🤖 Zone targeting on the wire
`zone_preview` accepts a `zones` config array (zone UUIDs or `"all"`, defaulting to `["all"]`), and `interactive_preview` accepts `target: {"zone": "<uuid>"}` alongside the existing `"active_scene"`. Both are optional with defaults matching the old behavior, so existing clients are unaffected.

### 🐛 Memberless zones no longer black out GPU scenes
A zone with layers but no outputs (the normal state when Studio creates a zone before devices join) failed projection admission, pushed the whole scene to CPU reconstruction, and then failed every frame with "CPU scene composition was not admitted" while publishing black. Zones that place nothing now project nothing, matching CPU raster behavior, and still render their own preview snapshot.

### 🔧 Scenes stop rebuilding renderers on every failed admission
`EffectPool::prepare_reconcile` built effect renderers as it walked layers, so a valid HTML layer ahead of an unregistered effect started and discarded a Servo page load on every retry frame. Layer resolution and control validation now complete for the entire scene before any renderer is constructed.

## 🤖 Zone Previews

- **Daemon:** `ZonePreviewSelection` (`All` / `Zones(Arc<[ZoneId]>)`) with `from_wire`, `includes`, and `union`; `ZonePreviewFrameReceiver::update_selection` lets a live subscriber narrow or widen its zones without reconnecting.
- **Relay:** `relay_zone_preview` filters frames before encoding and retires streams for dropped zones with a `preview_cancel` frame. A patched `zones` list re-walks the latest frames immediately.
- **Web UI:** `MainPreviewRequest` and `MainPreviewStep` (`Stop` / `Hold` / `Stream`) drive topic switching between `canvas` and `zone_preview`, unsubscribing the old topic before subscribing the new one. The preview holds rather than subscribing while a multi-zone scene document is still loading, so the patchwork never flashes.
- **Sidebar player:** step and apply now target the zone on screen. A non-Primary zone steps from its own top layer and applies via `ApplyTarget::Zone`; the scene canvas falls back to the page's quick-apply target.
- **Thumbnails and card art:** accent extraction and card attribution read `shown_zone_effect`, and `preview_frame_owner` only claims a frame when the shown zone's effect is its sole layer. The ignition pulse now keys on `(zone, effect_id)`, so switching zones refreshes the cabinet like an effect swap.
- **Interactive previews:** `InteractivePreviewTarget::Zone` renders one zone's layer stack on that zone's own canvas, with pointer input normalized into that zone's coordinates. GPU lanes now publish interactive frames correctly, and an in-flight GPU readback counts as a pending frame.

## 🔧 TUI and SDK

- `[` and `]` cycle the previewed zone in multi-zone scenes, in both the normal and fullscreen preview. The status line names the zone and its scene; cycling wraps and is a no-op below two LED zones.
- The TUI WebSocket client decodes `ZONE_PREVIEW_FRAME_TAG` (`0x08`) and its wide variant (`0x0c`) into `WsMessage::ZonePreview`, and a `watch::Receiver<PreviewTarget>` retargets the live subscription without a reconnect. Frames from the previous target are dropped before the re-subscribe lands.
- Switching scenes clears a stale zone focus via `AppState::set_active_scene`, so the preview never tracks a zone that no longer exists.
- **Python:** `open_interactive_preview(..., target=...)` now accepts `str | Mapping[str, str]`, so `target={"zone": zone_id}` renders one zone. The default stays `"active_scene"`; existing calls are unchanged.

## 🐛 Render Pipeline Fixes

- **Pause, stop, and sleep darken zone previews.** `publish_static_zone_previews` pushes the hold frame to every scene zone outside the normal cadence, covering idle entry, forced static sleep snapshots, and the late sleep frame. A paused zone's chip stays dimmed and off card art, and a zone rendering nothing previews dark via `with_dark_inactive_zone_previews`. All of it shares one static surface, so there is no per-zone encode cost.
- **Warn-once failure logging.** New `render_thread/failure_log.rs` adds `FailureLog<K>` with `note`/`clear`. A persistent scene render failure, effect failure, or projection composition failure logs once on the state change and reports the frame count on recovery, instead of publishing duplicate `LayerHealthChanged` events every frame and flooding the web UI.
- **CPU backing admitted on demand.** `admit_cpu_scene_fallback` and `admit_cpu_scene_surface_pool` allocate CPU targets when a GPU-admitted scene loses its textures or its projection fails, warning once per switchover. The next GPU-resident reconciliation drops them again.
- **Zone resources survive a failed frame.** A failed scene render keeps the failing scene's zone resources admitted and releases only the black-frame outputs, in-flight display finalizations, and a retained frame from an earlier dependency. Older scenes' resources are released on a scene switch.
- **Stopping ends a frame in flight.** A stop's black frame now finalizes the frame, and `OutputOverride::Stopped` triggers the late sleep frame.
- A scaled readback whose GPU composition fell back now fails instead of returning mismatched pixels.

## 🔒 Dependencies and CI

- Moved `tokio` to **1.54.1** and `ctutils` to **0.4.5** past new RustSec advisories, and patched `crypto-bigint` to **0.7.6**.
- **RUSTSEC-2026-0387** is waived in `deny.toml` for the unfixable `crypto-bigint 0.5.5` copy, which reaches the tree only through `webrtc-dtls 0.12` → `elliptic-curve 0.13`. The Hue driver restricts DTLS to `TLS_PSK_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`, so no ECDHE or ECDSA arithmetic runs on secrets. The waiver drops when `webrtc-dtls` moves to `elliptic-curve 0.14`.
- Every Linux CI job now pins **`ubuntu-24.04`** instead of `ubuntu-latest`, and `.github/actions/rust-build-cache/configure.mjs` adds `runnerKey` so Linux sccache prefixes include the runner image. Caches from different glibc baselines no longer collide.
- Test determinism: the allocation contract runs on the process main thread with `harness = false` (libtest's channel waiter was allocating 144 bytes inside measurement windows); the display face cadence test judges the mean interval across eleven writes rather than one gap that Windows timer jitter could shrink; and the failed-frame finalization test defers the GPU resolve with a test hook so it behaves the same on llvmpipe and real adapters.

## 📝 Documentation

- `docs/content/api/websocket.md` documents `zone_preview.zones` and zone-targeted `interactive_preview`, including pointer behavior and what happens when a named zone leaves the scene.
- `docs/content/guide/tui.md` covers one-zone previews and the `[`/`]` keys.
- README drops stale macOS release language and repeated platform detail, and curl install instructions now point at the udev rules commands.

## Upgrade Notes

- No wire breakage. `zones` defaults to `["all"]` and `target` defaults to `"active_scene"`, so clients that send neither keep their current behavior.
- Clients sending `zones` to an older daemon get a `validation_error` naming `config.zone_preview`; the web UI and TUI both detect this and fall back to the scene canvas automatically. Custom clients should handle the same case.
- Embedders using the remote bridge see a new optional `zone` field on `PreviewDemand`. Ignoring it streams the scene canvas as before.
- Self-hosted CI runners on older Ubuntu images should move to 24.04 to match the new build baseline.
